name: Provence

climate: Grenache, Syrah and Carignan sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

keyfacts: Côtes de Provence is the largest Provence appellation, followed by Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence and Coteaux Varois en Provence, and together they make 96% of Provence AOC wine.
Red Bandol must age at least 18 months in casks or large wooden vats, and the wines are built for long keeping.
The mistral, a cold, dry and often violent north wind, helps keep the vines healthy by curbing disease.
Cassis AOC is unusual in Provence because white wine makes up about 70% of its production.

notes: Provence is known mainly for rosé, which is normally dry, with zesty acidity.
Many wines carry the scents of the garrigue: wild lavender, rosemary and thyme.
Some Provence wines resemble Southern Rhône wines, sharing grapes and some of their style.

blurb.text: A region of southeast France where wine has been made for at least 2,600 years, since the Greeks founded Marseille. It holds Bandol, Cassis, Bellet and Côtes de Provence.
